title: Platform systems & services - playbook, runbooks, dashboards, roadmap, and team wiki (addendum Q3 2026)
author: Ava Thompson
body:
Purpose
-------
This addendum updates the canonical Platform Systems & Services playbook with Q3 2026 operational changes, new alert templates, and a short retrospective from the June platform reliability exercise. It is intended as an incremental update to the main playbook and runbook index.

Summary of changes
------------------
- New alert suppression policy for maintenance windows and large-scale model rollouts.
- Revised inference-runtime remediation steps when autoscaling stalls under burst traffic.
- Grafana dashboard layout update: added cost-per-token panel and model-level latency heatmap.
- Short retrospective: platform reliability exercise (2026-06-18) findings and action items.

Alert suppression policy (maintenance & rollout windows)
------------------------------------------------------
1) Purpose: reduce alert noise during planned maintenance and model rollout storms while preserving P1 detection.
2) Rules:
   - Maintenance windows must be declared in the alerting repo via a `maintenance_windows.yaml` entry with owner, start/end, and affected services.
   - Suppression TTL: default 2 hours, extendable by owner with justification.
   - P1 overrides: availability and data-loss alerts are never suppressed.
3) Workflow: before a rollout, create a maintenance PR referencing the change and the targeted alert IDs. Observability-team will approve and merge.

Example suppression entry (ops/alerts/maintenance_windows.yaml)
```
- id: model-rollout-us-west-2-2026-07-15
  owner: runtime-team
  services: [inference-runtime, cache-proxy]
  start: "2026-07-15T09:00:00Z"
  end: "2026-07-15T12:00:00Z"
  reason: "Large model canary and traffic migration"
```

Inference-runtime: autoscale stall remediation (new steps)
---------------------------------------------------------
1) Detect: cluster-level GPU utilization high but pod autoscaler not launching new pods and queue depth increasing.
2) Quick checks:
   - Verify HPA/VPA status: `kubectl get hpa -n runtime` and `kubectl describe hpa <name>`
   - Check cluster autoscaler events: `kubectl get events -n kube-system | grep cluster-autoscaler`
   - Confirm node group scaling limits in cloud console and capacity pools (dedicated vs shared).
3) Mitigation sequence:\   - If HPA misconfigured: temporarily scale replica count: `kubectl scale deploy inference-runtime --replicas=<n>` and open follow-up PR to fix HPA config.
   - If cluster autoscaler at limit: unblock by adding temporary burst nodes to the dedicated pool or moving tolerant models to preemptible nodes.
   - If scheduling failures due to taints/tolerations: remove taint or add toleration for the runtime placeholder pods.
4) Verification: ensure queue depth reduces and tail latency returns to p95 baseline within 15 minutes.

Dashboard updates
----------------
- New panel: Cost per token by model and by route (daily rolling 24h). Query: `sum(cost_tokens_total) by (model)` with unit conversion.
- New heatmap: model-level latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) across regions.
- Folder reorg: Grafana folder `Platform / Services` split into `Platform / Services - Core` and `Platform / Services - ML` for clearer ownership.

Operational exercise retrospective (2026-06-18)
-----------------------------------------------
- Scope: simulated regional outage for us-east-1 causing increased latency and partial node loss.
- Findings:
  1. Failover automation performed correctly for api-gateway, but smart-routing delay for model variants was ~7 minutes due to stale routing cache.
  2. Alert suppression prevented noise but also delayed awareness of a secondary metrics-collector backlog.
- Action items:
  - Short term: reduce routing cache TTL to 30s and add cache invalidation hook in deployment-orchestrator (owner: runtime-team). Target: 2026-07-10.
  - Medium term: implement forward-pressure signal in metrics-collector that surfaces backlog warnings to PagerDuty (owner: observability-team). Target: 2026-09-01.
  - Complete: update suppression policy to include an automatic metrics sanity check before full suppression acceptance. Target: 2026-08-01.

Runbook clarifications added
--------------------------
- api-gateway runbook: added step to verify WAF rate-limiting logs and correlate with CloudFront/edge metrics.
- inference-runtime runbook: added explicit fallback ordering for model variants (fallback -> smaller-quantized -> locality-fallback).
- metrics-collector runbook: added disk-pressure preflight and TSDB compaction checks.

Quick reference: new alert templates (examples)
----------------------------------------------
1) InferenceRuntimeAutoscaleStall (P1)
- expr: `sum(kube_node_status_capacity_gpu) - sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests_gpu) < 1 and increase_over_time(queue_length[10m]) > 0`
- for: 10m
- severity: page
- annotations: summary: "Possible autoscale stall in inference-runtime", runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/inference-runtime-autoscale-stall-2026.json"

2) MetricsCollectorBacklog (P2)
- expr: `rate(prometheus_tsdb_index_size_bytes[5m]) > 0 and prometheus_local_wal_corruption_total > 0`
- for: 5m
- severity: warn
- annotations: summary: "TSDB backlog or write failures detected", runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/metrics-collector-backlog-2026.json"

Knowledge base links (appendix)
------------------------------
- Alert suppression implementation: git@repo.redwood.com:ops/alerts-suppression.git
- Grafana changes: internal Grafana PRs referenced in team wiki folder `Platform / Services`
- Routing cache config: /confluence/eng-platform/runtime-architecture/cache-config-guidance-2026.json

How to use this addendum
------------------------
- This document is an incremental update; link it from the primary playbook and update the runbook index entry.
- Owners must close action items in the roadmap tool and tag this doc in their sprint tickets.

Contact
-------
Ping the author (@Ava Thompson) or the reviewers list for questions. For urgent operational issues, use #platform-ops and the platform-oncall rotation.
